key_insight: Long-horizon LLM RL can fail because small token-level policy errors compound into large trajectory-level state distribution shifts, and TAPO explicitly corrects for this gap.
engineering_relevance: For building stable reasoning agents, TAPO offers a more reliable optimization strategy than token- or sequence-only RL methods when rollouts get long.
method: Derives a trajectory-aware state-distribution correction from the off-policy policy gradient.
Uses a geometric-mean estimator to reduce variance during training.
Applies length-aware dynamic clipping to limit overly deviated trajectory updates.
evidence_signal: The paper reports experiments on eight competition-level benchmarks, with improvements of up to 48% over GRPO on mathematical reasoning and 12% on algorithmic coding, plus better training stability.
watch_item: The added trajectory correction, variance estimator, and dynamic clipping likely increase implementation complexity and may require careful tuning for different rollout lengths.
paper_title: Trajectory-Aware Policy Optimization: Closing the State Distribution Gap in Long-Horizon LLM RL
